name: OpenVibe.Watch
tagline: Watch anything. Hear about what matters.
description: OpenVibe.Watch checks a web page, an RSS or Atom feed or a JSON API on the cadence you pick, pulls out the value you care about, and tells you when it changes or crosses the line you set — politely: it asks sites whether anything changed before reading them, spaces its requests per site and waits when a site asks. Next: events and webhooks, browser checks, prices and releases, cameras on your own network, and actions for your apps and agents.

pillars.title: Any source
pillars.text: Pages, feeds, APIs, repos, videos, streams and cameras.

pillars.title: What changed
pillars.text: Extraction, diffs and conditions, with AI summaries when you want them.

pillars.title: Anywhere it matters
pillars.text: Notifications, events, webhooks and agent triggers.

pillars.title: Respectful and safe
pillars.text: Site terms, robots rules and fair limits on every check.

faq.question: What can I watch today?
faq.answer: A web page (all of it, or the part a CSS selector or a pattern picks), an RSS or Atom feed (for example a GitHub releases feed), or a JSON API and a path into it.

faq.question: How often does it check?
faq.answer: Every 15 minutes, hourly, every 6 hours or daily — your choice. It never checks faster than that, backs off when a site fails, and waits when a site asks it to.

faq.question: How will I hear about a change?
faq.answer: When your condition fires, a notification arrives on your OpenVibe account, and the watch page shows every check and the value it found.

faq.question: Does it hammer the sites it watches?
faq.answer: No. It sends the site's own validators first, so an unchanged page costs no body, keeps a minimum gap between requests to one site, and records every check.

faq.question: Is it free?
faq.answer: Yes, while it is in alpha.

keywords: website change monitoring, uptime monitoring api, price drop alerts, restock alerts, release monitoring, youtube video analysis, security camera alerts
